newsitem.title: INDONESIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indonesian newspapers - Feb 5.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indonesian newspapers - Feb 5.

text.p: The following are the leading stories in the Indonesian press on February 5. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

Home Affairs Ministry has said campaigners should have a police permit and that any written material to be used during the election campaigns scheduled for April should be screened by the election commission. Three political parties, the ruling Golkar, the United Development Party (PPP) and the Indonesian Democratic Party (PDI) will contest the general elections in May.
Indonesia will announce today its 200 millionth citizen after a baby is chosen and named by President Suharto from the more than 8,000 babies delivered across the country on Tuesday.

Indonesia has said it understands Malaysia's decision to close a dozen border crossing points along the Sarawak - Kalimantan boundary after the recent riot in West Kalimantan province, on the Indonesian side of Borneo island.
Indonesia's state-owned gold and nickel company PT Aneka Tambang has said it has told the government it was interested in taking part in the Busang gold find.
The army chief of staff General R. Hartono has reiterated the military's stance to take repressive action against rioters.
